agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider updated Public Safety Committee terms of reference
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council will consider approving an amended Terms of Reference (TOR) for the Public Safety Committee at its October 6, 2026 meeting. The updated rules would merge the existing four Community Safety Advisory Committees (CSACs) into two larger ones — one north and one south — by combining districts one and two, and districts three and four. The change is meant to address declining volunteer engagement and improve knowledge sharing across districts. There are no financial implications for the change.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Check the October 6, 2026 council agenda if your business relies on the Public Safety Committee's work or you want to comment on the proposed changes.

key_dates.label: Burnaby Public Safety Committee TOR decision meeting

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider new Burnaby Neighbourhood House funding agreement
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council will consider a new 3-year contribution agreement with the Burnaby Neighbourhood House Society (BNHS) running January 1, 2027 to December 31, 2029, totalling $324,000 — $100,000 cash plus up to $8,000 in-kind annually (up from $5,000). BNHS may allocate funds among its subsidiaries (Burnaby Meals on Wheels, Burnaby Christmas Bureau, Burnaby Community Services Society, Burnaby Seniors Outreach Services Society). BNHS remains ineligible for other Community Grants during the term but can still apply for permissive tax exemptions and lease grants.
agenda_briefs.action_required: If your business partners with BNHS or its subsidiaries, note the new agreement term starts January 1, 2027 and BNHS cannot apply for additional Community Grants during it.

agenda_briefs.title: Burnaby Council to consider Fall 2026 community grant recipients
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council will consider approving recommended Fall 2026 community grant recipients across Recreational Sport, Operating, Initiative, Subsidized Use, and In-Kind categories. Recommended amounts include $10,000 for Burnaby Fellowship Centre Society, $2,500 for Volunteer Grandparents Society, $10,000 for Volunteer Burnaby, $12,500 for Centre Canada Newcomer Services Society, $10,000 for LaPower Running Society, $7,000 for L'Arche Foundation, $2,650 for Lower Mainland Purpose Society, $6,556 for Metro Minor Ball Hockey, $12,000 for Odd Squad Productions, $5,000 for Salvation Army Cariboo Hill Temple, $2,597 for Prostate Cancer Support Group, $5,293 for Royal Canadian Legion Branch 83, $8,318.26 for Branch 148, $25,000 for Burnaby Hospital Foundation, and $10,000 for United Way. No decision has been made yet.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Check the meeting agenda and appendices to see if your organization is on the recommended list, and watch for Council's decision.

agenda_briefs.title: Burnaby Council to consider 2026 Pat Quinn Classic sport hosting grant
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council will consider an off-cycle request from Robyn Hughes (Tourism Burnaby/Sport Burnaby) for a 2026 Pat Quinn Classic Sport Hosting Grant, submitted late through Burnaby Minor Hockey Association after the regular deadline was missed due to a volunteer's unexpected health circumstances. The 2026 tournament runs December 27–31. In 2025 it drew 55 teams (including from the US and Japan), over 1,700 Burnaby room nights, and an estimated $2.1 million in economic impact. Council has not yet decided.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Watch for Council's decision on the off-cycle 2026 Pat Quinn Classic grant — if approved, expect more tournament visitors in Burnaby December 27–31.

agenda_briefs.title: Proposed: Burnaby Council to Meet Privately on Land and Award Matters
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council is set to hold a closed meeting where the public will be excluded, under Sections 90 and 92 of the Community Charter. Council will consider two items behind closed doors: personal information about an identifiable individual being considered for a municipal award or honour (or who offered a gift on condition of anonymity), and the acquisition, sale, or expropriation of land or improvements where disclosure could harm the municipality's interests. No decisions or bylaw changes are proposed in this agenda item, and no details about the specific land or individual are being released.
